title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter and token/event ordering for streaming structured output (OpenAI compat)
author: Lucas Ortega
description: Fixes an ordering bug in the SSE streaming encoder that could emit partial JSON fragments with delimiters in the wrong order when streaming structured outputs (function/tool calling and partial-json responses) and under heavy batching. Root cause: the sse encoder split token emission and delimiter/event emission across two buffers which could be flushed out-of-order when partial JSON objects and token-level events interleave. This manifested as corrupted partial JSON payloads, broken function call reconstruction on the client, and intermittent invalid JSON when using the OpenAI compatibility layer. Changes: unify the emission path so token bytes and event delimiters are serialized in a single sequence, introduce an explicit end-of-event sentinel to guarantee deterministic flush ordering, add safeguards around multi-part JSON objects so the "delta" fragments for function calls are always emitted in-order, and update the openai_compat stream adapter to map internal event tuples to OpenAI-style "delta" events without reordering. Adds a focused test suite reproducing several flaky cases, a fuzz harness for additional regression coverage, and a canary job that validates fixes against streaming infra. Also updates docs/streaming.md with guidelines for partial JSON-safe tokenizers. See commits and reviewers below. Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] integration canary [x] docs updated [x] regression fuzz harness [x] changelog entry
